findings.title: Cancelled HTTP requests can expose a late native failure instead of cancellation
findings.trigger: Start a cancellable request, cancel its signal, then reject pending http_request IPC with network-error, request-timeout or response-too-large.
findings.effect: The catch branch does not recheck cancellation. It exposes network-error/request-timeout/ResponseTooLargeError despite cancel_request being sent. Native select and frontend settlement can race, so callers cannot consistently identify a deliberately cancelled operation. No UI retry or live playback consequence is asserted by this probe.
findings.suggestedNextAction: In a separate repair task, normalize a cancelled signal before mapping a late rejection. Retain native cancellation/finally cleanup and add permanent regressions for late network/timeout/size failures and unchanged normal error mapping.

findings.title: Ordinary binary HTTP still crosses IPC as a JSON number array
findings.trigger: A built-in/native loopback HTTP read requests responseType=bytes.
findings.effect: Rust converts the byte vector to serde_json::Value; renderer receives number[] then allocates Uint8Array again. The body limit defaults to 16 MiB and permits up to 512 MiB, so it does not bound additional per-byte JSON representation/IPC encoding allocations. This violates the maintained raw-binary Response/buffer-view convention. No measured peak-memory figure or demonstrated playback failure is asserted.
findings.owner: apps/tauri/src-tauri/src/network/http.rs + model.rs HTTP DTO and apps/tauri/src/platform/native-http.ts
findings.suggestedNextAction: In a separate native/renderer repair, carry byte bodies with a bounded raw IPC Response and typed buffer view while retaining status/headers, account identity, size-recovery errors and cancellation. Update bytes contract tests and verify a real native binary fixture.
